children.text:
AI is the tool that will suck up all this data from the 3rd party that is storing and selling it. Let's curtail data leakage before it reaches that point. Loose lips sink ships.

Speaking of AI, when people using ARTEX [1] break into these vendors that aggregate all the voice, video and voice transcripts how many conversations by governors, congress members, national intelligence will the hackers find and what might they do with such potentially embarrassing gems?

[1] - https://www.artex.sh/forks

I think what a lot of people don't seem to get with these sorts of "yes, TV was bad too" analogies is that the difference between AI and previous technologies often isn't qualitative. It's quantitative. If one could assign a magnitude or speed to tech, TV or cameras maybe would be 20. But AI is closer to 200.

To use a car analogy, your argument is along the lines of "what's wrong with banning driving at 300MPH? We let people go 30MPH, then 40MPH, then 50MPH just fine!"

That's a good start. Now include any device that transmits pictures, videos, voice or voice transcripts anywhere. Televisions, toys, appliances, automobiles, toasters, action cams, drones, as a child could be present around any of those. Yes those other devices too.

All it would really take is one of these devices recording classified conversations or something really embarrassing to a member of congress to curtail this evil pattern. Classified conversations are supposed to legally take place in a SCIF but as most of us know they also happen on consumer chat platforms and around the dinner table.

title: New York Ban AI Toys for 5 Years
